name: Img
comment: Img provides convenient functions to support image operations on HTML Canvas and [`CanvasSpace`](#link). Combine this with other Pts functions to experiment with visual forms that integrate bitmaps and vector graphics.

signatures.comment: Create an Img

parameters.name: editable
parameters.comment: Specify if you want to manipulate pixels of this image. Default is `false`.

parameters.name: space
parameters.comment: Set the `CanvasSpace` reference. This is optional but will make sure the image's pixelScale match the canvas and set the context for creating pattern.

parameters.name: crossOrigin
parameters.comment: an optional parameter to enable loading cross-domain images if set to true. The image server's configuration must also be set correctly. For more, see [this documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/CORS_enabled_image).

accessors.name: ctx
accessors.comment: Get the internal canvas' context. You can use this to draw directly on canvas, or create a new [CanvasForm](#link) instance with it.

accessors.name: current
accessors.comment: Get current image source. If editable, this will return the canvas, otherwise it will return the original image.

accessors.name: imageSize
accessors.comment: Get size of the original image

accessors.name: loaded
accessors.comment: Get whether the image is loaded

accessors.name: scaledMatrix
accessors.comment:
Get a Mat instance with a scale transform based on current `pixelScale`.
This can be useful for generating a domMatrix for transforming patterns consistently across different pixel-density screens.

signatures.comment: Get an efficient, readonly bitmap of the current canvas.
signatures.returns_comment: a Promise that resolves to an ImageBitmap

parameters.name: size
parameters.comment: Optional size to crop

signatures.comment: Remove the elements and data associated with this Img.
Crop an area of the image.

parameters.name: box
parameters.comment: bounding box

signatures.comment: Apply filters such as blur and grayscale to the canvas image. The original image is unchanged until `sync()`.

parameters.name: css
parameters.comment: a css filter string such as "blur(10px) | contrast(200%)". See [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/filter#browser_compatibility) for a list of filter functions.

signatures.comment: Get a CanvasForm for drawing on the internal canvas if this Img is editable
Initiate an editable canvas

parameters.name: width
parameters.comment: width of canvas

parameters.name: height
parameters.comment: height of canvas

parameters.name: canvasScale
parameters.comment: pixel scale

signatures.comment: Load an image.
signatures.returns_comment: a Promise that resolves to an Img

parameters.name: src
parameters.comment: an url of the image in same domain. Alternatively you can use a base64 string. To load from Blob, use `Img.fromBlob`.

signatures.comment: Create a canvas pattern for `fill()`

parameters.name: reptition
parameters.comment: set how the pattern should repeat-fill

parameters.name: dynamic
parameters.comment: If true, use this Img's internal canvas content as pattern fill. This enables the pattern to update dynamically.

signatures.comment: Get the RGBA values of a pixel in the image
signatures.returns_comment: [R,G,B,A] values of the pixel at the specific position

parameters.name: p
parameters.comment: position of the pixel

parameters.name: rescale
parameters.comment: Specify if the pixel position should be scaled. Usually use rescale when tracking image and don't rescale when tracking canvas. You may also set a custom scale value.

signatures.comment: Resize the canvas image. The original image is unchanged until `sync()`.

parameters.name: sizeOrScale
parameters.comment: A PtLike array specifying either [x, y] scales or [x, y] sizes.

parameters.name: asScale
parameters.comment: If true, treat the first parameter as scales. Otherwise, treat it as specific sizes.

signatures.comment:
Replace the image with the current canvas data. For example, you can use CanvasForm's static functions to draw on `this.ctx` and then update the current image.
To display the internal canvas, you can also use `form.image( img.canvas )` directly.
